name: Empedocles
bio: Empedocles is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no firm date for the poet.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 569).

poems.title: Book IX, 569: From his book “On Nature”
poems.author: Empedocles
poems.note: Paton marks the second part with the remark “(From his Purifications)”.
poems.text: I have been a boy and a girl, a shrub, a bird, and a warm-blooded fish of the sea. Hail! my friends who dwell in the citadel of the great city, yellow Agrigentum, observers of righteousness. Know that I, no longer a mortal, but an immortal god, sojourn here honoured by all as is meet, crowned with fillets and flowery garlands.
